Kitchen countertops in Weston: quartz or granite in a Florida kitchen? Quartz, for most people. It is engineered, so it is non-porous. It never needs sealing and it does not stain from oil or wine. Granite is natural stone and needs resealing, which people forget about until there is a mark. Marble is the one to think hardest about. It etches from lemon and anything acidic, and in a kitchen used every day it will show. Honest note: quartz can discolour under long direct sun, so it is worth a thought for a counter under a big west window or in an outdoor kitchen. Granite handles sun better. Design and construction come from one team here, so the counter gets decided with the cabinets instead of after them. Licensed and insured general contractor, License #CGC-1506284. Kitchen countertops in Weston: quartz or granite in a Florida kitchen? Quartz, for most people. It is engineered, so it is non-porous. It never needs sealing and it does not stain from oil or wine. Granite is natural stone and needs resealing, which people forget about until there is a mark. Marble is the one to think hardest about. It etches from lemon and anything acidic, and in a kitchen used every day it will show. Honest note: quartz can discolour under long direct sun, so it is worth a thought for a counter under a big west window or in an outdoor kitchen. Granite handles sun better. Design and construction come from one team here, so the counter gets decided with the cabinets instead of after them. Licensed and insured general contractor, License #CGC-1506284. From the owner
An older home doesn't necessarily need to lose its character to gain the functionality homeowners want today. Successful remodeling can preserve the qualities that make a home distinctive while thoughtfully improving the way its spaces work. For some Denver-area homes, that might mean creating a better connection between the kitchen and living area. For others, it could involve improving storage, reworking an awkward floorplan, updating cabinetry or introducing materials that complement the home's architecture while giving the interior a fresh direction. At Christopher’s Kitchen & Bath, we approach remodeling with both the existing home and the homeowner in mind. Rather than automatically following current trends, we consider proportion, flow, architectural details, materials and how each design decision contributes to the larger space. If your home has character worth keeping but spaces that no longer meet your needs, start a conversation with our design team about creating a remodel that respects the past while working beautifully for life today.
